Container.Name: StoryEngine
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted LLM storytelling server.
PRIVATE IMAGE. This package is not public, so unraid must be logged in to ghcr.io with a token that can read packages before this template will pull. Without that the pull fails with a 404 that reads like a typo.
CHANNEL. This template follows the testing channel: every tagged alpha moves it, so unraid's update check offers each one. To stay on one build, change the repository tag to that build's version, such as ghcr.io/bureaucromancer/storyengine:1.0.0-alpha.6. There is no latest.
FIRST RUN. The container binds 0.0.0.0, because a container's own loopback is unreachable however you map the port. That means the create-the-first- admin screen is reachable from your LAN the moment it starts, so it asks for a setup token. It is in the container log on every start until the first admin exists, on the line that says "needs this setup token", and it is also the contents of state/setup.token in the data folder. Copy it, then use the WebUI button.
DATA. Everything the install is — accounts, library, sessions, config — is under /data. Back that up; nothing else needs backing up. The container runs as uid 1000, not as root: if Docker created the appdata folder it is root-owned and the server refuses to start, saying so. Run chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/storyengine once, on the host.
ALPHA. There is no compatibility promise between alpha builds. An older build will refuse to open a data directory a newer one has written, rather than migrating it.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: The port the UI and the API are both served on. One process, one port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Accounts, library, sessions and config.json. The container runs as uid 1000, so this folder must be writable by it — if Docker created it, it is root-owned: run chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/storyengine once on the host.

Config.Name: Bind address
Config.Description: Where the server listens inside the container. 0.0.0.0 is correct here and is the same variable a bare-metal install would use — the image is not a different build. Setting it to 127.0.0.1 makes the container unreachable however you map the port.

Config.Name: Supervised
Config.Description: Whether something will start this container again if it stops. The --restart=unless-stopped under Extra Parameters does, so 1 is correct here — it is what lets the settings page offer Restart now instead of explaining that the server does not restart itself (09 §6.4). unraid's Autostart is not the same thing: it starts containers when the array starts, and restarts nothing that exits. Nothing inside a container can detect this for itself, which is why it is a variable rather than a guess. Set it to 0 if you remove the --restart parameter.
